findings.issue: The contract says tenantId comes from the active core RequestContext, or else from a verified request.tenantId 'installed by tenancy middleware'. No such middleware exists. Under the TEN-01 contract, the pre-guard RequestContext holds only requestId, startedAt and locale; tenantId is patched in after guards by RequestContextInterceptor and TenantContextInterceptor, both interceptors. So at guard time, request.tenantId is set only by an auth guard that already ran: AuthContextGuard (header resolver plus entitlement, packages/backend/src/auth/auth-context.guard.ts:144-155) or StynxAuthGuard (verified stynxClaims.tenantId). On public-tenant routes both guards delete it. The contract never says the auth guard must run before the global AuthorizationGuard. Nest runs APP_GUARDs in registration order, and every APP_GUARD runs before any @UseGuards(StynxAuthGuard). With global:true, a decorated route in an app using the controller-level auth guard (as the auth package's own controller does) would therefore have no principal and no tenant. Tests that pre-seed request.tenantId or principal would still pass, while real composition fails or delivers tenantId undefined.
findings.required_change: Replace the provenance sentence with the real guard-time sources: request.tenantId set by AuthContextGuard after entitlement, or by StynxAuthGuard from verified session claims. Say explicitly that a Host-selected public tenant is undefined at guard time. Require global:true to run after an authentication APP_GUARD, and document the registration order (for example, import the auth module before StynxAuthorizationModule.forRoot({global:true})). Add Inspector A sensors that use the real AuthContextGuard and StynxAuthGuard as APP_GUARDs, in both orders, with no pre-seeded request fields. One order must show that the principal and tenant reach the evaluator. The other must show the documented failure or deny. Also assert that an X-Tenant-Id header with no auth-guard verification leaves tenantId undefined.

findings.issue: The switch path the contract describes is not the one STYNX uses. StynxAuthController POST /sessions/switch calls StynxAuthService.switchTenant, which calls exchangeExistingIdentity to create a new session first and then revokes actor.sid (packages/auth/src/auth.service.ts:79-95). SessionService.exchange has no production caller. The contract adds priorSessionId but does not require switchTenant to pass actor.sid, check that the prior session belongs to the same user and is active, or define ordering. It also leaves three cases open: reject-new on a switch into the same tenant (the actor's own active session would block it), exclusion of the prior sid from the conflict set, and atomic revoke-prior-plus-create. It does not say whether the new session inherits strongFactorVerifiedAt, so a second switch would fail. For single-session, 'denial before revoke' is stated only for strong factor, and exchange() currently revokes before create.
findings.required_change: Name StynxAuthService.switchTenant/exchangeExistingIdentity as the trusted switch boundary. It must pass priorSessionId = actor.sid and verifiedFactor only from validated claims. SessionService must check that prior's owner, active state and marker before any write. The single-session atomic operation must take the prior sid: exclude it from conflicts, and revoke it and create the new session in one atomic step. That removes the separate post-create revoke, or fixes its order so no failure leaves both or neither session active. The strongFactorVerifiedAt marker is copied from the prior session, not refreshed. State that every policy denial (strong factor, reject-new) happens before any revoke or create in create, exchange and switchTenant. Update prompts 41 and 43 to require HTTP sensors for /sessions/switch covering these cases (same tenant and cross-tenant, reject-new, revoke-existing, and a second chained switch).

findings.issue: The strong-factor model does not match the upstream requirement or the DETRAN consumer. UPS-SES-02 asks for a configurable claim ('claim amr/acr configurável'). DETRAN's DetranSessionStrongFactorGuard reads a configurable claim name (STYNX_STRONG_FACTOR_CLAIM, default amr), accepts array or string values split on whitespace or commas, and compares case-insensitively. The contract hard-codes the amr array and the acr string with exact values, so a Cognito access token carrying amr as a string (for example from a pre-token-generation customization) would be rejected as malformed. The DETRAN consumer then cannot migrate without a shim.
findings.required_change: Pin the claim model explicitly, either as configurable claim names or as defined amr/acr parsing. Cover string versus array handling, the delimiter, case normalization, the acr multi-value rule, and validation of empty configuration at boot. Add Inspector B sensors for each accepted and rejected shape. If this deliberately departs from DETRAN, record it for the §7 conformance-table deviation column, with Owner visibility, before dispatch.

findings.issue: 'Prior active session' is undefined for the atomic policy. RedisSessionStore sets key TTL only at the absolute expiresAt. Idle-expired sessions stay in Redis with status active until SessionService.get notices them, and the user index can hold stale sids (pruneIndex is not atomic). A Lua or MULTI policy that checks only key existence or status would make reject-new lock a user out for up to absoluteSeconds after an idle timeout. revoke-existing must also reproduce every side effect of revokeSession (delete the key, clean the user and tenant indexes, mark the refresh lookup 'used') in the same atomic unit.
findings.required_change: Define active as status active, expiresAt later than now, and idleExpiresAt later than now, using the service clock value passed into the store operation. Require the Redis operation to be one server-side script, or WATCH/MULTI with retry, that reads the user index, filters by tenantId and activeness, applies the mode, and performs the full revokeSession key effects plus createSession writes. Mirror and invalidation publishing happens after commit from the returned revoked records. Add sensors: an idle-expired prior does not block reject-new; concurrent creates across N parallel clients leave exactly one active session per user and tenant in real Redis; after revoke-existing, the old refresh token fails on refresh.

findings.issue: The readiness indicator cannot reliably report a disconnected Redis as down. node-redis queues commands while reconnecting (offline queue enabled, created in redis-session-store.ts:47), so a read-only probe through SessionStore hangs rather than failing. StynxHealthService.readiness awaits every indicator in Promise.all with no timeout, so /health readiness would hang. SessionStore also has no probe method, so createSessionStoreReadinessIndicator(store) has no defined operation. Nothing assigns ownership of a test that composes with the real StynxHealthModule: sessions has no @stynx-nyx/health devDependency, and adding one edits packages/sessions/package.json and the lockfile and requires package-readmes:write.
findings.required_change: Specify the probe: an optional read-only store method or a fixed getSession of a sentinel key, bounded by a configurable timeout (with a default) that returns down with a safe reason; for Redis, also report down immediately when client.isReady is false. Require a sensor that stops or pauses the real Redis container, not just calling quit(), and asserts down within the timeout, then up again after reconnect. Choose where the StynxHealthModule.forRoot(options,[indicator]) composition test lives. If it lives in sessions, assign the devDependency, lockfile and package-readmes:write to the maestro Engineer before Inspector B runs, and add them to the plan's lock and gate list. Otherwise place it in reference/api without touching the frozen reference/api/package.json.

findings.issue: Wildcard semantics are underspecified, and current case handling diverges. The backend lowercases roles and permissions (default-policy-evaluator.ts). Angular hasAllPermissions/hasAnyPermissions compare exactly and case-sensitively. The contract says 'same semantics' without choosing a case rule. It does not say whether an intermediate prefix such as ops:case:* is allowed, and it does not say that a '*' on the required side is literal and never matches granted permissions. stynxPermissionGuard and the auth package's PermissionGuard (@Permission) are not mentioned.
findings.required_change: Pin the case rule for permissions on both platforms, the multi-segment prefix behavior (ops:case:* grants ops:case:read but not ops:caser), and that wildcards apply only to granted values. State whether stynxPermissionGuard inherits the new semantics (it calls hasAllPermissions) and whether the auth PermissionGuard stays exact, recording that as a deliberate difference. Add presence and absence sensors for each rule.

findings.issue: The deny-envelope and resolver-target sensors are vague. 'deny factory' does not require asserting full HTTP status and body under StynxErrorFilter, for example 401 with a consumer code when the principal is missing and 403 with a consumer code on a denied target, the forms DETRAN's TEAT and RAIT envelopes take. Partial resolver results ({} or resource only) and a throwing evaluator or onDeny are not covered. DETRAN skips when either resource or action is absent, but the contract fills the missing property from the class or handler name.
findings.required_change: Require exact status and JSON body assertions for onDeny returning an HttpException and a core StynxError, with and without a principal, on a decorated route and a resolver-only route. Define and test how undefined, {} and partial targets behave. Define whether evaluator and onDeny exceptions propagate unchanged.

findings.issue: The locks and release obligations are incomplete. Inspector A's lock names 'specs de autorização' but not packages/contracts/test, which prompt 40 allows. The plan does not produce the C-0002 §7 conformance-table row (published version, real symbols, tests, deviations) for UPS-AUTHZ-01…07 and UPS-SES-01…03. It does not say whether reference/api exercises the new options.
findings.required_change: List exact lock paths per worker, including packages/contracts/test if used. Add a maestro Architect task to record the §7 conformance row, using real 1.5.0 symbols and every deviation from the proposal. State whether reference/api is intentionally left on defaults so that ci:reference-apps proves only compatibility.

summary: Most of the contract fits STYNX's current code: the authorization module and guard, the default-evaluator binding, the Redis store shape and the health indicator API. Default-preserving opt-in is the right approach. Five blocking gaps remain. (1) The tenant source at guard time is misattributed to a middleware that does not exist, and the order of the global guard relative to the auth guard is unspecified. (2) The real tenant-switch path (StynxAuthService.switchTenant, which creates the new session before revoking the old one) is not covered by the single-session and strong-factor rules. (3) The strong-factor claim model departs from UPS-SES-02 and the DETRAN consumer. (4) 'Active' is undefined for the atomic Redis policy, so idle-expired sessions could block logins. (5) Redis readiness can hang, and nobody owns the health composition test or its dependency. All five are repairable in the contract and prompts; no worker should be dispatched until they are fixed.
